summary: The appeals challenge the High Court's judgment convicting the appellants under Section 302 IPC and Section 25 of the Arms Act, while acquitting them of Section 307 IPC. Key issues included reliability of eyewitnesses, prosecution's failure to examine an injured witness (Om Prakash), admissibility of evidence from investigating officer PW-13 who was not fully cross-examined, and forensic linkage between recovered weapons and the crime. The prosecution relied on oral and documentary evidence, including FSL reports linking seized arms to the offense. The defense argued discrepancies in recovery and chain of evidence, and alleged screening of a crucial witness. The Court emphasized evaluation of 'matters before it' under Section 3 of the Evidence Act, distinguishing between belief in fact existence and prudence-based probability. It upheld the High Court’s balanced assessment of evidence, including partially hostile testimonies and forensic findings.
legal_provisions_cited: State of Orissa v. Prasanna Kumar Mohanty, (2009) 7 SCC 412
Santa Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1956 SC 526
Anter Singh v. State of Rajasthan, (2004) 10 SCC 657
Jagir Singh v. State (Delhi Administration), 1975 CrLJ 1009
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed; conviction under Section 302 IPC and Section 25 of the Arms Act upheld, with life imprisonment confirmed.
